    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.regularModule_indecomposable_of_idempotents {R : Type v} [Ring R] [Nontrivial R] (hidem : ∀ (a : R), a * a = a → a = 0 ∨ a = 1) :

    If a nontrivial ring has no nontrivial idempotents, its right regular module (presented as a left module over the opposite ring) is indecomposable.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.isLocalRing_of_finite_of_idempotents {k : Type u} [Field k] {R : Type v} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [Nontrivial R] (hidem : ∀ (a : R), a * a = a → a = 0 ∨ a = 1) :

    A finite-dimensional nontrivial algebra with no nontrivial idempotents is local. This is obtained by applying the finite-dimensional Fitting theorem to its indecomposable right regular module.

        Module.Finite k (CategoryTheory.End F)

        If the indexing category has finitely many objects and all values of a module-valued functor are finite-dimensional, then its endomorphism algebra is finite-dimensional. Naturality cuts out a subspace of the finite product of the component endomorphism spaces.

        A functor on a category with finitely many objects, all of whose values are finite-dimensional vector spaces, is a finite biproduct of indecomposable functors. The induction measure is the sum of the component dimensions.
